title: Kaikeyi's boons
hook: Rama rides to his coronation through cheering streets, and finds his father unable to speak

segments.voice: Yesterday: Kaikeyi's boons, and the longest night. The king begged, and she held him to satya, his sworn word. Did you notice a promise that costs you little? Today, morning comes. Day five hundred twenty-two.

Outside the palace, nobody knows. The sun comes up on the morning Ayodhya has been preparing for. Vasishtha arrives with his students and the sacred waters. The streets are full. Bards are singing outside the king's door to wake him, the way they do every morning. Inside, the king hasn't slept, and he can't stand up. Two worlds, separated by one wall, and in a moment Rama is going to walk from one into the other.
screen: `OUTSIDE, NOBODY KNOWS.` → `BARDS SING AT THE KING'S DOOR.` → `TWO WORLDS, ONE WALL.`

segments.voice: The charioteer Sumantra goes in to tell the king everything is ready. The king can barely speak. It's Kaikeyi who answers. Go and bring Rama here. Sumantra, puzzled, goes. Rama comes by chariot through streets packed with people, and he hears them as he passes. Today he'll be made heir. Look how fortunate we are. Women lean from windows to see him. He walks into Kaikeyi's room and finds his father on a couch, pale, beside the queen. Rama bows to his father's feet, and then to Kaikeyi's. The king manages one word, Rama, and then his eyes fill and he can't say anything more. Rama is frightened. He has never seen his father like this. He turns to Kaikeyi. Have I done something wrong? Is he ill? Has someone hurt him? Kaikeyi says the king won't speak because he's afraid to tell you something unpleasant. He made me a promise. If you'll do what he's promised, I'll tell you. And Rama, without knowing what's coming, says something he can't take back. At my father's word I would walk into fire. I would drink poison. Tell me what he wants. I promise to do it, and Rama doesn't say things twice. So Kaikeyi tells him herself, plainly. The two boons. Bharata to be consecrated with the waters made ready for Rama. Rama to the Dandaka forest for fourteen years, in bark clothes, with matted hair. Notice who says it. Not the king. The king lies there, unable to speak. The boons are delivered in Kaikeyi's voice, to a son who has just promised to obey.
screen: `SUMANTRA SENT TO FETCH RAMA.` · `THE KING SAYS ONE WORD: RAMA.` · `RAMA PROMISES BEFORE HE KNOWS.` · `KAIKEYI TELLS HIM HERSELF.` · then, large: `RAMA DOESN'T SAY THINGS TWICE.`

segments.voice: Sit and settle. Bring back a moment just before hard news, if you've had one: the room, the faces, the silence. Breathe in slowly, and let the body brace a little, the way it does. Then breathe out and let the bracing go. Do that again, gently. You're practicing the moment before, so that when it comes, you can meet it standing. The bell holds the time.
Kaikeyi's boons, delivered. The king can only say Rama's name, so Kaikeyi tells Rama herself: Bharata crowned, and fourteen years in the forest.
Your line: Kaikeyi's boons. Today, if someone you love can't find the words, be patient with the silence. Day five hundred twenty-two.

howItsDone: In the text, Rama's phrase that he does not say things twice comes before he knows what he has agreed to; it is a picture of a person whose word is final.

myth: Dasharatha tells Rama the news himself
he can only say one word, Rama; Kaikeyi tells him.
Rama promises to obey before he knows what's asked
fire or poison, he says, and he doesn't say things twice.
the city already knows about the boons that morning
outside, the crowds are still celebrating.

fork.setup: you're Rama. your father can't speak, and the queen says she'll explain only if you promise to obey. what do you say?
options: first tell me what it is.
I promise; Rama doesn't say things twice.
fork.reveal: Rama promises at once: at his father's word he would walk into fire or drink poison.

original.note: Sanskrit pratijñā: a promise, a vow. Rama gives one before he hears what it will cost.

trapdoor: what you thought: the king sends Rama away himself.
what it means: the king can't speak, and Kaikeyi tells Rama the boons.
what a scholar hears: Rama's half-verse about not speaking twice is spoken before he knows the cost, so his promise binds him the way his father's oath bound the king.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda 14–17 (dawn; Sumantra sent; Rama's ride through the city)

Fire and poison in Rama's promise: confirm wording.
